title: Agentic GraphRAG: Simplifying Retrieval Across Structured & Unstructured Data — Zach Blumenfeld
talk_summary: Zach Blumenfeld demonstrates building a knowledge graph from unstructured resumes plus structured HR data, then giving an agent schema-aware tools (MCP server that reads schema and generates Cypher) so it can answer aggregation, similarity, and collaboration questions that plain vector search fails at. The core lesson is that a small, explicit data model plus query tools beats semantic search for analytical and relational questions.

takeaways.technique: Explicit schema/data-model in agent instructions plus schema-reading query tool
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of only a vector-search tool, they give the agent a description of the data model and an MCP server that reads the schema and generates Cypher queries, so the agent can do aggregations and traversals rather than top-k similarity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I tell it a little bit about my data model in here and then I'm actually going to be using this MCP server that allows it to read the schema and also generate cipher statements.
takeaways.numbers: Vector-only search returned 'five Python developers' (K=5 artifact); graph query returned 28 developers

takeaways.technique: Predefined parameterized query tools alongside LLM-generated queries
takeaways.what_they_do: Beyond letting the model generate queries on the fly, they register fixed tools for common traversals (e.g. find similar people within N hops, find collaborators in domains) so common questions hit tested queries.

takeaways.technique: Entity extraction into a typed graph with enumerations
takeaways.what_they_do: They run LLM extraction with Pydantic classes and enums (accomplishment types, domains, work types) to turn documents into typed nodes/edges, giving a controllable, auditable model rather than raw text chunks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I use paidantic classes to do that. So I have concept of enumerations on the types of accomplishments and domains

takeaways.technique: Schema-flexible graph for evolving data models
takeaways.what_they_do: Adding many-to-many relationships (collaboration) required only new edges in the graph, versus a join-table refactor in an RDBMS.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in a tabular environment is I would have to create another join table ... But the great thing about graph is that I don't have to do that at all.
